name: Black Breath
label: Southern Lord
lede: A Bellingham crust-punk band picked up Boss HM-2 pedals, worshipped Swedish death metal, and became one of the loudest things Seattle exported in the 2010s.

eras.title: Bellingham basements
eras.text: Black Breath starts in a college town north of Seattle, plays house shows and puts out its own first EP. The sound is crust and hardcore with Swedish death metal buzzsaw guitars laid on top.

years.h: Zack Muljat and Jamie Byrum start Black Breath in Bellingham
years.p: Per Grokipedia, guitarist Muljat and drummer Byrum founded the band in winter 2005, with [[Neil McAdams|ceeaf6f3-14d9-4097-8b69-3f0d997148fa]] on vocals. The name nods to a Repulsion song that [[Entombed|61b99cc4-06cd-4ad5-9bac-950b2daef9cc]] later covered, and to Tolkien.

years.h: Eric Wallace and Elijah Nelson join
years.p: Guitarist Wallace arrives and Nelson takes over bass, completing the lineup that will make the Southern Lord records (dates per Grokipedia).

years.h: Razor to Oblivion EP, on their own Hot Mass label
years.p: The band's first record is a short, fast EP put out through its own Hot Mass Records. It is what gets Southern Lord interested.
years.xp: Sources give the date as January or November 2008, and describe it as four or five tracks. Southern Lord signed the band in October 2009 and the EP was later reissued on the label.

years.h: Black Breath moves down to Seattle
years.p: The band relocates from Bellingham to Seattle in early 2008, according to Grokipedia.

eras.title: Signed by Southern Lord
eras.text: Sunn O)))'s label, home of Sunn O))) and Goatsnake, signs the band, and Black Breath goes to Massachusetts to record with Kurt Ballou.

years.p: The Los Angeles label, run by [[Greg Anderson|a8da7651-6d6f-4021-98a6-d68b35b1e4f8]], adds the Seattle band to its roster and reissues the Razor to Oblivion EP.

years.h: Heavy Breathing, cut at GodCity with Kurt Ballou
years.p: The debut album is recorded in Salem, Massachusetts by [[Kurt Ballou|1e922902-2cb9-499f-aeb5-9a8c51dd0df0]] of [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]], and it puts the Boss HM-2 guitar tone front and center.
years.xp: Twelve tracks, produced by Ballou at his GodCity Studio. Ballou would record all three of the band's Southern Lord albums.

years.h: First national tours with Trap Them and others
years.p: In 2010 the band tours the US behind the album, per Wikipedia sharing bills with acts including Victims, Rise and Fall and [[Trap Them|b24b6ae8-333e-4351-b3b7-6be843195a16]].

eras.title: Sentenced to Life
eras.text: A lineup change on guitar, then the record that made the band's name in the metal press.

years.h: Founding guitarist Zack Muljat leaves, Mark Palm steps in
years.p: Grokipedia says Muljat left to pursue law and Mark Palm replaced him around 2011-2012.
Ten songs including "Home of the Grave" and "Mother Abyss," again made with Kurt Ballou at GodCity.
years.xp:
The band told Bara Metal that they nearly stopped at nine songs, then added "The Flame" at the last minute, and that much of the lyric writing happened in hotel rooms between 2 and 5 AM. A harmonized guitar part on "Of Flesh" ate an afternoon for barely a second and a half of music; the band joked it was the "$200 riff."

The cover shows Wallace's hand holding a sledgehammer.

years.p: The band owns several of the pink Boss HM-2 pedals that defined Swedish death metal's guitar sound, and says they are central to how it writes riffs.
years.xp: Ghost Cult and AllMusic name Entombed's Wolverine Blues era, Poison Idea and Discharge as core influences.

eras.title: Slaves Beyond Death
eras.text: The band tours hard and makes a third album that leans toward old-school heavy metal.

years.h: Third album announced; recorded in winter at GodCity
years.p: Southern Lord announces the new record. Kurt Ballou again produces in Salem, Massachusetts.

years.h: Slaves Beyond Death shifts toward heavy metal
years.p: Eight songs. Drummer [[Jamie Byrum|51713a0f-9469-4ff5-9153-46125816e75f]] told Ghost Cult the guitar playing is more rooted in old-school metal and hard rock than death metal.

eras.title: Quiet, then a loss and a box set
eras.text: The band goes silent after 2015, and Elijah Nelson's death closes the story.

years.p: Blabbermouth reported he died over the weekend of December 28-29. The cause was not made public. Nasum called him "the Cliff Burton of death metal."

years.h: Southern Lord releases a vinyl box set of the discography
years.p: Grokipedia reports a comprehensive box set gathering all the band's records.

sources.title: Bara Metal on Sentenced to Life
